Two independent inherited records point the same way (memory_86: shorter onboarding lifted completion and time-to-value; memory_31: fewer required signup fields gave a durable SMB activation lift), which is why I want the archived source for exactly those two rather than for the tempting alternative. I am deliberately not choosing promotional_pricing despite the competitor's entry pricing: memory_73 reports a 31% conversion and 18% revenue lift but a 12-point later-cycle retention loss under an unchanged support model, so the headline gain is partly borrowed from future revenue and conflicts with the sustainable-qualified-revenue objective; discounting into a price war would also likely repeat that pattern at larger scale. activation_messaging (memory_91) is the credible runner-up and would be my fallback if verification undercuts the onboarding records. referral_incentive (memory_57) worked on established customers, not the SMB acquisition funnel that is actually bleeding, and enterprise_sales_assist (memory_44) addresses a segment that is not the source of the decline.
